game: CIN@BAL Week 13 2025 / 2025-11-27 20:20 ET / BAL -7 / total 52.5 / outdoors, weather not saved

script.base: Baltimore is a 7-point home favorite (implied 29.8-22.8) in a 52.5 outdoor night game, so the book expects BAL to lead by about a score, not a 17-point blowout. Base flow: BAL ahead at half, Henry carries the clock late, Jackson mixes Flowers and Andrews; CIN trails and stays pass-heavy because Higgins is out, with Chase/Iosivas and Brown checkdowns keeping the dog in the 20s. Starters should finish.
script.flip1: BAL jumps up 17+ early, kills the clock, and Henry's carries spike while CIN abandons the run. Brown's rush share dies and only checkdowns remain; if it is truly out of hand he can be pulled for Perine and the 71.5 rush+rec leg fails.
script.flip2: CIN hangs around or leads (turnovers, slow BAL start, or a shootout). BAL throws, Henry's rush line is the one that dies (his 64-yard recent game is the template), and CIN skill volume (Chase, Iosivas, Brown receiving) is the side that clears.

pre_mortem: Monday both overs lost. Brown: Cincinnati was down multiple scores by the second quarter, the run was abandoned, Higgins' targets became two Chase shots instead of checkdowns, and Perine took the late snaps, so Brown finished in the neighborhood of his 37-yard rush game plus a quiet receiving night and missed 71.5. Henry: the 5.22 YPC Bengals defense was a pass funnel in this game, Jackson kept the QB-run share he already showed (15 carries in the L3), Mitchell took the explosives with Hill out, the game stayed close so there was no clock-kill, and Henry landed on 18 carries for about 61, under 71.5. That counter is stronger against Henry (lean) than against Brown (the combined floor is 105), which is why Henry is a lean and why Iosivas over 22.5 was not added: his last4 includes a 0, the Higgins vacuum may already be priced into Chase's 92.5, and there is no coverage map.
